calibration_disclosure: The calibration gate (Task 1c, docs/findings/Sprint4-calibration-gate.md) used n=12-16 and specific seeds (base 200). Those data SUGGESTED H_I6b; per owner ruling, calibration data may suggest but only FRESH data confirms. All verdicts below run on fresh instance draws (disjoint seeds) at densities pinned here in advance.

H_I6a_binary_at_face_value.status: the SEALED I6 from prereg_v4/v5, scored EXACTLY as posed — no refinement, no rescue.
H_I6a_binary_at_face_value.hypothesis: the bounded-width (localization) oracle predicts smoother measured solution-space terrain: bounded-width-P rows read smoother than affine-unbounded-P rows.
H_I6a_binary_at_face_value.decision_rule: direction = sign(mean ruggedness of affine arm - mean ruggedness of bounded arm); permutation p over the both-real (localization, ruggedness) rows with the fixed harness (permute localization labels among both-real rows; hand-count selftest in CI); floor >= 12 concordant rows.

verdict.SUPPORTED: direction bounded-smoother AND p<0.05 AND floor met AND instrument qualified
verdict.NOT_SUPPORTED: floor met + instrument qualified, but direction null/reversed or p>=0.05
verdict.INSTRUMENT_NOT_QUALIFIED: Vega fails (it does NOT — it passed)

H_I6a_binary_at_face_value.owner_expectation_on_record: the calibration +0.11 separation with the wide bounded-arm spread (0.83-0.93) will likely read NOT SUPPORTED or weakly-directional. Report AT SIZE; no rescue. 'Width-as-a-binary predicts terrain' appears wrong in its strong form — this goes in the F1 predictions ledger next to the k in {3,4} miss.
H_I6a_binary_at_face_value.ledger: record H_I6a's verdict in the F1 canon-or-computation ledger as a scored prediction (hit/miss), like P1-P4 and the Factors k-prediction.

H_I6b_polymorphism_ordering.status: NEW sealed hypothesis (Mendeleev-gallery treatment): calibration-SUGGESTED, confirmed here on FRESH data at pre-pinned densities. Exploratory in origin, sealed before the confirmation run.
H_I6b_polymorphism_ordering.hypothesis: measured solution-space ruggedness is ORDERED by the tractability-giving polymorphism, not by the width bit: semilattice(Horn/min-max) < majority(2-SAT/bijunctive) < order/median <= affine. I.e. localization-as-specific-polymorphism structures terrain where localization-as-width does not.
H_I6b_polymorphism_ordering.decision_rule: on FRESH draws (disjoint seeds), at BOTH pinned densities (0.7*alpha_c and 0.9*alpha_c per family), compute each arm's mean ruggedness with both samplers (concordant). CONFIRMED iff the arm-mean ordering semilattice < majority < order/median <= affine holds (strict where stated) AND is STABLE across both density points AND both samplers. Report the per-arm means + a rank statistic.

verdict.CONFIRMED: ordering holds and is stable across both densities + both samplers
verdict.PARTIAL: ordering holds at one density or up to one adjacent-arm swap
verdict.NOT_CONFIRMED: ordering does not hold on fresh data

H_I6b_polymorphism_ordering.the_anomaly_is_the_headline: the finding-shaped object is NOT the gradient per se but the ANOMALY: order-3/median-3 are BOUNDED-WIDTH yet read affine-rugged. The sealed sub-claim: bounded-width families SPLIT into smooth and rugged sub-populations by polymorphism type. Confirm the split (Horn-family smooth vs order/median rugged) on fresh data.

density_protocol.matched_density_definition: RELATIVE, not absolute: per family, empirically locate the satisfiability threshold alpha_c (the density where random instances transition SAT->UNSAT), THEN measure at 0.7*alpha_c and 0.9*alpha_c. Cross-family comparison is at matched fraction-of-threshold.
density_protocol.alpha_c_location: a pre-run bisection/scan per family estimates alpha_c (fraction of satisfiable instances crossing 0.5); logged per family before the confirmation run.
density_protocol.robustness_requirement: an ordering/verdict counts as confirmed ONLY if stable across BOTH 0.7 and 0.9 fraction-of-threshold points. This converts the density-sensitivity caveat into a robustness gate.

R25_in_spirit_novelty_netting.rule: before claiming novelty, net the theory-ANTICIPATED component. Document what prior structure theory predicts and subtract it; report only the residual as the finding.
anticipated: Horn solution sets are lattices (closed under min) -> connectivity/consensus expected -> smooth is NOT novel
affine solution sets are cosets of a linear subspace -> dispersion/spread expected -> rugged is NOT novel
residual_novelty: the QUANTITATIVE ordering across bounded-width polymorphisms
ABOVE ALL the ANOMALY: order-3/median-3 bounded-width yet affine-rugged — no folklore hands you 'bounded-width splits into smooth and rugged sub-populations by polymorphism type'
R25_in_spirit_novelty_netting.writeup_frame: frame Sprint 4's landscape finding around the ANOMALY, not the gradient.
